label: copy phase: outputting x / h / i / l
explanation: Output-token detector during the copy phase. About 91% of activation mass falls in the copy phase (t > L), and the main driver is the token being output: when out_tok is x, h, i or l the unit is active on about 44-47% of those steps (8.5-9.4x lift), and those four tokens alone carry about 74% of the mass. Weaker, graded secondary tokens are 1 (3.9x), v and d (about 2.2-2.5x); m and n are suppressed. It is strongest at recall positions 2-5 and weaker on the first output (recall_idx 1) and the last one. The top examples (around 0.9-1.0 of max) are copy steps outputting i, h, x or n early in the copy, and activity often spills onto neighbouring copy steps whose next output is one of these tokens. It rarely fires in the original phase (8% of mass, mostly t = 0..2) or on the delimiter step. As a predicate it is incomplete: only about half of copy-phase x/h/i/l outputs are active, and adding next_out, position limits or the secondary tokens did not raise F1 above about 0.55.
